messages.subject: Multiple plots with shared legend
parts:
Hi All,

I've searched through the ggplot2 group to find some kind of answer to
how I might approach plotting multiple plots with a shared legend, but
haven't found a good solution to what I'm looking for. Essentially, I
want to plot 3 figures with a shared legend, where the legend would
appear at the bottom of the plot.

#This first function is just something I wrote so I don't have to
repeat myself.
plotf<-function(dat,blank,legend.position="right",title=""){
pl<-ggplot(dat,aes(x=statistic,y=Indice,shape=Diversity))+
geom_point(aes(fill=test,alpha=sig),size=3)+
scale_fill_hue(name="Matrix Association")+
scale_colour_hue(name="Matrix Association")+
geom_point(aes(color=test),size=3)+
scale_shape_manual(values=c(21,22,24),name="Beta
Diversity",labels=c("Taxnomic","Terminal Phylogenetic","Basal
Phylogenetic")) +

scale_alpha_manual(values=c(0.08,0.6,1),name="Significance",labels=c(expression(p>=0.05),expression(p<0.05),expression(p<0.005)))
+
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
facet_grid(Data~B)+
#theme_bw()+

eval(parse(text=paste("opts(",paste(blank,"=","theme_blank()",collapse=",
"),")",sep="")))+
opts(legend.position=switch(legend.position,
right="right",
left="left",
bottom="bottom",
top="top",
none="none"
))+
opts(title=title)

return(pl)
}

#I applied the plotf function to three subsets of my data,
"cd.all","cd.east", and "cd.west"; the "blank" command just specifies
which opts parameters should be equal to "theme_blank()"
plA<-
plotf(cd.all,blank=c("panel.grid.major","panel.grid.minor","strip.text.y","strip.background"),title="All")
plE<-
plotf(cd.east,blank=c("panel.grid.major","panel.grid.minor","axis.text.y","axis.title.y","strip.text.y","strip.background"),title="East")
plW<-
plotf(cd.west,blank=c("panel.grid.major","panel.grid.minor","axis.text.y","axis.title.y","strip.background"),title="West")

#Loading some relevant libraries recommended for use by other users in
ggplot2
library(gridExtra)
library(devtools)
library(reshape2)

#Script to keep the legend box from one of my plots (doesn't matter
which one, since they all share the same one)
leg <- ggplotGrob(plA + opts(keep="legend_box"))
legend=gTree(children=gList(leg), cl="legendGrob")
widthDetails.legendGrob <- function(x) unit(2.5, "cm")

#Some code I found on the forum that suggested who store the legend
information and reprint it
leg <- ggplotGrob(plA + opts(keep="legend_box"))
legend=gTree(children=gList(leg), cl="legendGrob")
widthDetails.legendGrob <- function(x) unit(2.5, "cm")

#Everything here worked awesome except for the last command to print
the legend. It simply prints "legendGrob[GRID.legendGrob.1427]" into
the R Console.
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow=2, ncol=3,
widths = unit(c(6,6,6), "cm"),
heights = unit(rep(6, 1), "cm"))))
print(plA + opts(legend.position="none"), vp = viewport(layout.pos.row
= 1, layout.pos.col = 1))
print(plE + opts(legend.position="none"), vp = viewport(layout.pos.row
= 1, layout.pos.col = 2))
print(plW + opts(legend.position="none"), vp = viewport(layout.pos.row
= 1, layout.pos.col = 3))
print(legend, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1:3))

Any suggestions?

messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with shared legend
parts:
Hi All,

Figured out the solution:

library(gridExtra)
tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(plA))
leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]

grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(plA + opts(legend.position="none"),
plE + opts(legend.position="none"),
plW + opts(legend.position="none"),
main ="this is a title",
left = "This is my global Y-axis
title",ncol=3), legend,
widths=unit.c(unit(1, "npc") - legend$width,
legend$width), ncol=2)
